name: Exposing AI-generated Videos Dataset
description: The generative model has made significant advancements in the creation of realistic videos, which causes security issues. However, this emerging risk has not been adequately addressed due to the absence of a benchmark dataset for AI-generated videos. In this paper, we first construct a video dataset using advanced diffusion-based video generation algorithms with various semantic contents. Besides, typical video lossy operations over network transmission are adopted to generate degraded samples. Then, by analyzing local and global temporal defects of current AI-generated videos, a novel detection framework by adaptively learning local motion information and global appearance variation is constructed to expose fake videos. Finally, experiments are conducted to evaluate the generalization and robustness of different spatial and temporal domain detection methods, where the results can serve as the baseline and demonstrate the research challenge for future studies.
evaluation_method: AUC (ROC), accuracy and F1 for fake vs. real video detection
reputation: A newly introduced dataset targeting detection of diffusion-based AI-generated videos; useful as an early benchmark in video-forensics research but not yet widely standardized.
notes: Contains videos from diffusion-based generative models and degraded (lossy) variants to test robustness; likely to age as generative models improve; temporal and compression artifacts are important factors; non-LLM benchmark.
